points.text: Central claim that AR avoids spurious edits unsupported; GPT-Over not superior
No locality/preservation metric outside edit region
No controlled AR-vs-diffusion comparison with same data and backbone
Baselines old and weak; recent strong editors missing
Primary GPT-Balance metric self-constructed, single judge run, quantised, no variance
No human evaluation or agreement with GPT scores
Resolution differences and resizing for judge unstated
Headline gains relative on custom metric; CLIP gains small or absent
GPT judge may favour outputs resembling GPT-4o-derived training data
SAR motivation rests on single attention heatmap example
No ablation of SAR layer placement or simpler alternatives
SAR ablation single setting and seed, modest gains, no error bars
Scale-mismatch explanation unverified; non-scale-aligned control missing; abstract overclaims
Efficiency comparison at unequal settings; timing setup undescribed
Memory and token counts not reported
No comparison to distilled or few-step diffusion editors
Scaling claim confounded by codebook dimension and training schedule differences
Limitations (resolution, multi-turn edits, failures) not discussed
Tokenizer reconstruction error on preserved regions not measured
Novelty moderate: Infinity fine-tuning plus one extra first-layer reference
Training-free VAR editing cited but not compared
Effect of VLM data filtering not ablated
Reproducibility depends on model release; filtered data not released
No reasoning-based or multi-step editing experiments (e.g., WISE, GEdit)
Attention heatmap analysis missing for the tuned model
GPT-score evaluation may be biased; human study needed to validate
No comparison against frontier editors (GPT-4o-Image, FLUX.1 Kontext, Qwen-Image)
'First tuning-based VAR editor' claim false given NEP; VAR term misleading
Related work omits closely related contemporaneous editing models
No evaluation of generalization to unseen edit types or few-shot adaptation
Limited analysis of failure modes, e.g., global/text edits
Only CLIP and GPT metrics; no user study or error typology
Only two academic datasets; no out-of-distribution or real-world images
SAR formulation not mathematically precise (Down operator, masking, positional encoding)
Figure 2 omits components; heatmap colour scale unclear
Data filtering details and release unclear; code only after acceptance
No comparison with MLLM-based editing frameworks
SAR novelty modest, incremental extension
GPT-4o judge costly and proprietary; open-source VLM evaluation needed
Missing standard editing benchmarks ImgEdit and GEdit-Bench
Kimi-VL filtering non-reproducible; model quality may depend on it
